content: 1. Patients should take oral contraceptives at least one hour before administering exenatide. Exenatide may slow gastric emptying, potentially reducing the absorption and effectiveness of oral medications requiring rapid gastrointestinal absorption. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Ethinyl estradiol may decrease the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetic medications by impairing glucose tolerance. Patients with diabetes should be closely monitored for glycemic control. 3. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is recommended. Conversely, ethinyl estradiol may increase the levels or effects of fedratinib. Avoid coadministration with dual CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 inhibitors, as the interaction has not been fully studied. 4. Felbamate decreases ethinyl estradiol levels through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but monitoring is recommended. 5. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP2E1 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs, as fexinidazole also inhibits CYP3A4, increasing the risk of adverse effects with CYP3A4 substrates. 6. Fezolinetant levels and effects are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP1A2 inhibition. This combination is contraindicated. Fezolinetant exposure is further increased when coadministered with CYP1A2 inhibitors. 7. Finererone levels and effects are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor serum potassium levels during therapy initiation or dosage adjustments, and adjust finererone dosage as needed. 8. Flibanserin levels and adverse effects may increase when coadministered with ethinyl estradiol due to CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 9. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 10. Fluvoxamine levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP1A2 inhibition. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 11. Fosamprenavir may decrease the efficacy of ethinyl estradiol and alter hormone levels. Alternative nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 12. Fostemsavir increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Avoid coadministration or adjust the dose of BCRP substrates. Do not exceed an ethinyl estradiol dose of 30 mcg/day. 13. Frovatriptan levels may be increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP1A2 inhibition. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but monitoring is recommended. 14. Gemifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 16. Green tea levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol due to decreased elimination. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 17. Griseofulvin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 18. Hemin effects are decreased by ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Caution and close monitoring are advised, as drugs that increase delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase may further reduce hemin efficacy. 19. Heparin effects are decreased by ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of thromboembolic disorders. 20. Hyaluronidase effects may be reduced by estrogens, including ethinyl estradiol, when administered in large systemic doses. Patients may require higher doses of hyaluronidase for equivalent dispersing effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs, as idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor. 22. Iloperidone increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 23. Imipramine metabolism may be reduced by ethinyl estradiol, potentially increasing antidepressant serum concentrations and adverse effects. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but monitoring is advised. 24. Indinavir may alter estrogen plasma levels, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 25. Insulin aspart, degludec, detemir, glargine, glulisine, inhaled insulin, lispro, NPH, and regular human insulin effects may be reduced by ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Estrogens may impair glucose tolerance, necessitating close monitoring of glycemic control in diabetic patients. 26. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 27. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. Close monitoring is recommended. 28. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 29. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 30. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 31. Lamotrigine levels are decreased by ethinyl estradiol due to increased hepatic clearance. Combination oral contraceptives significantly reduce lamotrigine plasma concentrations, likely due to glucuronidation induction. Close monitoring is advised. 32. Lapatinib levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP3A4 inhibition. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 33. Larotrectinib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but monitoring is recommended. 34. Lemborexant levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP3A4 inhibition. Lower nightly doses of lemborexant are recommended when coadministered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage modifications. 35. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is recommended, as lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrate levels for up to nine months after the last subcutaneous dose. 36. Leniolisib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 37. Lesinurad decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended, as hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. 38. Letrozole effects are decreased by ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration, as letrozole should not be used concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 39. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 40. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 41. Liraglutide effects may be reduced by ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may decrease the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 42. Lixisenatide decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by delaying gastric emptying and inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least one hour before or 11 hours after lixisenatide administration. Close monitoring is recommended. 43. Lomitapide levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP3A4 inhibition. The lomitapide dose should not exceed 30 mg/day. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 44. Lonafarnib levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lonafarnib dose and closely monitor for arrhythmias and other cardiac events. 45. Lonapegsomatropin effects are decreased by ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral estrogens may reduce serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) response to growth hormone analogs, potentially requiring higher growth hormone doses. Close monitoring is recommended. 46. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, reducing hormonal contraceptive efficacy. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended.
